q24899.en: A casualty in shock must be laid on the ground and, if possible, with the legs raised.

explain.short: Lying down with raised legs sends more blood to the heart and brain. This is the right position for shock.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'con le gambe sollevate' (with the legs raised) is the correct anti-shock position.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: lie down, legs up

q24900.en: A casualty in shock must be covered as well as possible, so that they do not get cold.

explain.short: A person in shock loses body heat easily. Covering them keeps them warm and helps them.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'coperto' (covered) is right: keep the person warm.

sceneParams.caption: Cover a person in shock to keep them warm
lines: Do not let them get cold

q24901.en: A casualty in shock must be laid down, keeping the legs raised if possible.

explain.short: Lying flat with the legs up helps the blood reach the heart and brain. This is what you do for shock.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'disteso' (lying down) plus 'gambe sollevate' (legs raised): both are correct.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: lie flat, legs up

q24902.en: With a casualty in shock, you must make them walk, to restart their blood circulation.

explain.short: A person in shock must lie still, not walk. Walking makes shock worse and they could fall.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'farlo camminare' (make them walk) sounds helpful but is wrong: they must lie down.

sceneParams.caption: Never make a person in shock walk

q24903.en: A casualty in shock must be put in a sitting position.

explain.short: Sitting up makes it harder for blood to reach the brain. A person in shock must lie down with the legs raised.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'posizione seduta' (sitting position) is wrong for shock: lying down is right.

sceneParams.caption: Shock: lying down, not sitting

q24904.en: With a casualty in shock, you must give them little slaps on the cheeks and legs, to restart their blood circulation.

explain.short: Slapping does not help a person in shock. Lay them down, raise the legs and keep them warm.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'piccoli schiaffi' (little slaps) is a false remedy.

sceneParams.caption: No slaps: lay down and keep warm

q24905.en: With a casualty in shock, you must make them drink small amounts of spirits (strong alcohol).

explain.short: Never give alcohol to an injured person. Alcohol makes shock worse.
explain.rule: A person in shock (stato di shock) must lie down on the ground, with the legs raised if possible, and be covered so they do not get cold. FALSE: making them walk, sitting them up, slapping them, or giving them strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'superalcolici' (spirits): never give alcohol or drinks to a casualty.

sceneParams.caption: Never give alcohol to an injured person
lines: Lay down, legs up, keep warm

q24906.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must check whether they are still breathing by putting a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly.

explain.short: With a hand on the lower chest or belly you feel it move up and down. This tells you the person is breathing.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'verificare se respira' (check if they breathe) is the first thing to do.

sceneParams.caption: Unconscious: check the breathing
lines: Hand on lower chest or belly

q24907.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, they may be moved only if you are sure they have no injury to the spine.

explain.short: Moving a person with a spine injury can cause paralysis. So you move them only if you are sure the spine is not hurt.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'solo se si è certi' (only if you are sure): here 'solo' makes the statement correct.

sceneParams.caption: Move only if the spine is surely not hurt
lines: Move only if sure it is not

q24908.en: If a road casualty is unconscious and finds it hard to breathe, you must clear the nose and mouth of any blockage at once.

explain.short: Something in the mouth or nose can stop the air. Clearing them at once helps the person breathe.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'liberare subito' (clear at once): air must pass freely.

sceneParams.caption: Clear nose and mouth so air can pass
lines: Clear nose and mouth at once

q24909.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must check their condition often until the ambulance arrives.

explain.short: An unconscious person can get worse quickly. Check them often and stay with them until the ambulance comes.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'controllare spesso' (check often) until help arrives is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Check often until the ambulance comes

q24910.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must give them alcoholic drinks.

explain.short: An unconscious person must never be given anything to drink: they can choke. Alcohol is also harmful.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'bevande alcooliche' (alcoholic drinks): never give drinks to an unconscious person.

sceneParams.caption: Never give drinks to an unconscious person

q24911.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must hold their hands still.

explain.short: There is no reason to hold the hands. What matters is breathing: check it and keep the airways clear.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'bloccargli le mani' (hold the hands still) is a useless invented step.

sceneParams.caption: No need to hold the hands: check breathing

q24912.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must bandage their head.

explain.short: Being unconscious does not mean a head wound. You bandage only a wound you see; first check breathing.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'fasciargli la testa' (bandage the head) is not the rule for an unconscious person.

sceneParams.caption: Unconscious does not mean: bandage the head
lines: Bandaging the head: not the rule

q24913.en: If a road casualty is unconscious, you must put them in a half-sitting position.

explain.short: An unconscious person is not sat up. If they breathe and the spine is safe, they go on their side (safety position) so the airways stay free.
explain.rule: With an unconscious person (incosciente): check the breathing with a hand on the lower side of the chest or on the belly, clear the nose and mouth if breathing is hard, and check them often until the ambulance arrives. Move them only if you are sure the spine is not injured. FALSE: alcohol, holding the hands, bandaging the head, sitting them half up.
explain.trap: 'semiseduta' (half-sitting) is for a conscious chest injury, not for an unconscious person.

sceneParams.caption: Unconscious: not half-sitting

q24914.en: If a road casualty is conscious but has a chest injury, you must try to make breathing easier by putting them in a half-sitting position.

explain.short: With a chest injury, sitting half up makes breathing easier than lying flat.
explain.rule: With a chest injury (trauma della gabbia toracica): if the person is conscious, help them breathe by sitting them half up; press a deep visible wound at once with a clean cloth; stay with them until medical help arrives. FALSE: deep breaths, lying down with legs raised, standing up.
explain.trap: 'semi-seduto' (half-sitting) is right here because the person is conscious with a chest injury.

sceneParams.caption: Chest injury: half-sitting to breathe better

q24915.en: If a road casualty is conscious but has a chest injury with a visible, deep wound, you must press on it at once with a clean cloth.

explain.short: Pressing on a deep wound with a clean cloth slows the bleeding and keeps out dirt.
explain.rule: With a chest injury (trauma della gabbia toracica): if the person is conscious, help them breathe by sitting them half up; press a deep visible wound at once with a clean cloth; stay with them until medical help arrives. FALSE: deep breaths, lying down with legs raised, standing up.
explain.trap: 'comprimere subito' (press at once) with something 'pulito' (clean) is correct.

sceneParams.caption: Deep chest wound: press with a clean cloth

q24916.en: If a road casualty has a chest injury, you must assist them until medical help arrives.

explain.short: A chest injury can get worse. Stay with the person and help them until the doctors arrive.
explain.rule: With a chest injury (trauma della gabbia toracica): if the person is conscious, help them breathe by sitting them half up; press a deep visible wound at once with a clean cloth; stay with them until medical help arrives. FALSE: deep breaths, lying down with legs raised, standing up.
explain.trap: 'assisterlo fino all'arrivo' (assist until arrival): do not leave them alone.

sceneParams.caption: Stay with them until medical help arrives

q24917.en: If a road casualty has a chest injury, you must make them take deep breaths.

explain.short: Deep breaths hurt and can make a chest injury worse. Let them breathe calmly in a half-sitting position.
explain.rule: With a chest injury (trauma della gabbia toracica): if the person is conscious, help them breathe by sitting them half up; press a deep visible wound at once with a clean cloth; stay with them until medical help arrives. FALSE: deep breaths, lying down with legs raised, standing up.
explain.trap: 'profondi respiri' (deep breaths) sounds good but is wrong with a chest injury.

sceneParams.caption: Chest injury: no deep breaths

q24918.en: If a road casualty has a chest injury, you must lay them down with the legs raised.

explain.short: Lying with legs raised is the shock position. With a chest injury it makes breathing harder; half-sitting is right.
explain.rule: With a chest injury (trauma della gabbia toracica): if the person is conscious, help them breathe by sitting them half up; press a deep visible wound at once with a clean cloth; stay with them until medical help arrives. FALSE: deep breaths, lying down with legs raised, standing up.
explain.trap: 'gambe sollevate' (legs raised) is for shock, not for a chest injury.

sceneParams.caption: Chest injury: half-sitting, not legs up

q24919.en: If a road casualty has a chest injury, you must keep them standing up, to reduce the loss of blood.

explain.short: Standing does not reduce bleeding and the person may faint. Press on the wound and sit them half up.
explain.rule: With a chest injury (trauma della gabbia toracica): if the person is conscious, help them breathe by sitting them half up; press a deep visible wound at once with a clean cloth; stay with them until medical help arrives. FALSE: deep breaths, lying down with legs raised, standing up.
explain.trap: 'stare alzato' (stand up) with a false reason about less bleeding.

sceneParams.caption: Chest injury: do not keep them standing
lines: Press the wound with a cloth

q24920.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must not move the broken limbs.

explain.short: Moving a broken bone causes pain and more damage. Leave it still.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'non bisogna muovere' (you must not move): this is right.

sceneParams.caption: Do not move broken limbs

q24921.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must keep them still, without doing anything else.

explain.short: Keep the broken limb still (immobilise it) as it is. Other actions are for doctors.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'bloccarglieli' (keep them still) and 'senza altre manovre' (nothing else) are both right.

sceneParams.caption: Broken limb: keep it still, nothing more

q24922.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must cover any wounds with clean material.

explain.short: Clean material protects the wound from dirt and germs.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'materiale pulito' (clean material) is right for any wound.

sceneParams.caption: Cover wounds with clean material

q24923.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must keep them still and right after, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps.

explain.short: First immobilise the broken limb. Then, if the person shows shock, lay them down and keep them warm.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'misure anti-shock' (anti-shock steps) come after, and only 'se necessario' (if needed).

sceneParams.caption: First keep still, then anti-shock if needed

q24924.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must try to make them walk, to reduce the pain.

explain.short: Walking on a broken leg causes more pain and damage. The limb must stay still.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'farlo camminare' (make them walk) with a false reason: less pain.

sceneParams.caption: Broken limbs: never make them walk

q24925.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must ask them to move them, to judge the type of injury.

explain.short: Moving a broken limb causes more damage. Only doctors judge the injury.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'chiedergli di muoverli' (ask them to move them) is wrong: do not move broken limbs.

sceneParams.caption: Do not ask them to move a broken limb

q24926.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs with a bone sticking out, you must try to put it back into the tissues.

explain.short: Pushing a bone back causes more damage and infection. Cover it with clean material and wait for help.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'riposizionarlo' (put it back) is a medical job, not yours.

sceneParams.caption: Never push a bone back in

q24927.en: If a road casualty has broken arms or legs, you must give them a strong alcoholic drink.

explain.short: Never give alcohol to an injured person. It can make shock worse.
explain.rule: With broken limbs (fratture agli arti): do not move them, keep them still (immobilise them) and do nothing more; cover any wounds with clean material; then, if needed, use the normal anti-shock steps. FALSE: making the person walk, asking them to move the limb, pushing a bone back in, giving strong alcohol.
explain.trap: 'bevanda superalcolica' (strong alcoholic drink): never for an injured person.

sceneParams.caption: Never give alcohol to an injured person

q24928.en: If a road casualty is burnt and there are still some flames, you must put them out by smothering them, for example with a blanket.

explain.short: A blanket cuts off the air and the flames go out. Act at once.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'soffocandole' (smothering them) is the right way to put out flames on a person.

sceneParams.caption: Smother the flames with a blanket

q24929.en: If a road casualty is burnt, it is advisable not to remove clothes stuck to the burnt skin.

explain.short: Pulling off stuck clothes tears the skin and makes the burn worse. Leave them on.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'non togliere' (do not remove) is right for clothes stuck to the skin.

sceneParams.caption: Leave clothes stuck to burnt skin

q24930.en: To reduce the pain of burns, you should use cold water, if possible.

explain.short: Cold water cools the burn and reduces the pain.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'acqua fredda' (cold water) is right for burns.

sceneParams.caption: Cold water reduces burn pain

q24931.en: If a road casualty has burns on the body, you should cover them with clean, if possible sterile, material.

explain.short: Burnt skin gets infected easily. Clean, sterile material protects it.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'materiale pulito, possibilmente sterile' (clean, if possible sterile) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Cover burns with clean, sterile material

q24932.en: If a road casualty is burnt and there are still some flames, you must wait for them to go out by themselves before acting.

explain.short: Waiting lets the fire burn the person more. Put the flames out at once with a blanket.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'aspettare che si spengano da sole' (wait for them to go out): no, act at once.

sceneParams.caption: Do not wait: smother the flames at once

q24933.en: If a road casualty is burnt, you must always remove the parts of the clothes stuck to the skin.

explain.short: Pulling off stuck clothes tears the burnt skin. They must be left on.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) and 'togliere' (remove): the opposite of the rule.

sceneParams.caption: Never pull off clothes stuck to burns

q24934.en: If a road casualty is burnt, you must disinfect the burns with alcohol.

explain.short: Alcohol on a burn causes strong pain and damage. Use cold water and clean material.
explain.rule: With burns (ustioni): put out any flames by smothering them, for example with a blanket; do not pull off clothes stuck to the burnt skin; use cold water to reduce the pain; cover burns with clean, if possible sterile, material. FALSE: waiting for the flames to go out, always removing stuck clothes, cleaning burns with alcohol.
explain.trap: 'disinfettare con l'alcool' (disinfect with alcohol) sounds medical but is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: No alcohol on burns: cold water instead

q24935.en: After a road accident, the rescuer who steps in must assess the situation well, to protect the injured from other dangers.

explain.short: First look at the scene: traffic, fire, fuel. Then protect the injured, for example with the warning triangle.
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'valutare bene la situazione' (assess the situation well) is the first step.

sceneParams.caption: First assess the scene, protect the injured

q24936.en: After a road accident, the rescuer who steps in must assist the injured as well as they can, but without taking actions that need medical skills.

explain.short: Help as much as you can, but leave medical treatment to doctors.
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'senza ... iniziative di specifica competenza medica' (no medical actions) is the limit.

sceneParams.caption: Help, but leave medical acts to doctors

q24937.en: After a road accident, the rescuer who steps in must help the injured according to their own abilities and knowledge.

explain.short: Everyone must help, each as they can. You do what you know how to do.
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'secondo le proprie possibilità e conoscenze' (according to your abilities and knowledge) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Help as far as you are able

q24938.en: Anyone involved in a road accident must always leave the place where it happened, at once.

explain.short: Those involved must stop and help the injured. Leaving is a crime (failing to give help).
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'allontanarsi sempre e subito' (always leave at once): the opposite of the duty.

sceneParams.caption: Involved in an accident? Stop and help

q24939.en: In a road accident, you must only wait for help to arrive, without doing anything.

explain.short: Waiting is not enough. Protect the scene, call 112 and help the injured as you can.
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) and 'senza fare nulla' (doing nothing): wrong, you must act.

sceneParams.caption: Do not just wait: protect, call, help

q24940.en: In a road accident, the first thing the rescuer must do is identify the injured person, asking their first name and surname.

explain.short: The name is not urgent. First protect the scene and check breathing and bleeding.
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'la prima cosa' (the first thing): asking the name is not first.

sceneParams.caption: First safety and breathing, not the name

q24941.en: In a road accident, the rescuer must give medicines to the victim, if the rescuer has no specific medical skills.

explain.short: Only people with medical skills may give medicines. A normal rescuer never gives medicines.
explain.rule: After a road accident the rescuer (soccorritore) first looks at the scene to protect the injured from more danger, then helps them as well as they can, with their own skills, but without doing medical things that only doctors should do. FALSE: always leaving at once, only waiting and doing nothing, asking the name first, giving medicines.
explain.trap: 'somministrare farmaci' (give medicines): only doctors and medical staff do this.

sceneParams.caption: Never give medicines: that is for doctors

q24942.en: A state of shock can be caused by strong pain.

explain.short: Shock can come from strong pain. The body reacts strongly and the person can feel very ill.
explain.rule: Shock (stato di shock) can be caused by strong pain, a strong emotion (joy, anger), heavy blood loss or a strong trauma (a bad injury). Shock is dangerous for health. Statements with 'non' or 'mai' (never) about these causes are FALSE.
explain.trap: 'può essere causato' (can be caused): yes, strong pain is one of the causes.

sceneParams.caption: Shock can come from strong pain
lines: Lay down, legs up, keep warm

q24943.en: A state of shock can be caused by a strong emotion (joy, anger).

explain.short: Shock can come from a strong emotion. The body reacts strongly and the person can feel very ill.
explain.rule: Shock (stato di shock) can be caused by strong pain, a strong emotion (joy, anger), heavy blood loss or a strong trauma (a bad injury). Shock is dangerous for health. Statements with 'non' or 'mai' (never) about these causes are FALSE.
explain.trap: 'può essere causato' (can be caused): yes, a strong emotion is one of the causes.

sceneParams.caption: Shock can come from a strong emotion
lines: Lay down, legs up, keep warm

q24944.en: A state of shock can be caused by heavy blood loss.

explain.short: Shock can come from heavy blood loss. The body reacts strongly and the person can feel very ill.
explain.rule: Shock (stato di shock) can be caused by strong pain, a strong emotion (joy, anger), heavy blood loss or a strong trauma (a bad injury). Shock is dangerous for health. Statements with 'non' or 'mai' (never) about these causes are FALSE.
explain.trap: 'può essere causato' (can be caused): yes, heavy blood loss is one of the causes.

sceneParams.caption: Shock can come from heavy blood loss

q24950.en: Drinking alcohol makes driving less safe, because it can cause excitement and recklessness.

explain.short: Alcohol can cause excitement and reckless driving. That makes driving less safe.
explain.rule: Alcohol makes driving LESS safe: it can cause excitement and reckless driving, slower reflexes, sleepiness and less concentration and attention. Any statement saying alcohol makes driving safer, easier, removes tiredness, makes you more alert or improves your sight is FALSE.
explain.trap: 'meno sicura' (less safe) is right: excitement and reckless driving is a real effect of alcohol.

q24960.en: During driving, you must use glasses or contact lenses if the licence states that duty.

explain.short: If the licence says you need glasses or contact lenses, you must wear them every time you drive.
explain.rule: You must wear glasses or contact lenses while driving whenever your licence says so, written in words or as the EU code '01'. This applies always, on every road, day and night. FALSE: 'solo'/'soltanto' (only) at night, only in poor visibility, only on motorways, or only above 6 dioptres.
explain.trap: 'se nella patente' (if on the licence): the licence decides.
